question.prompt: In the set of equations \(z^x=y^{2x},\) \(2^z=2\cdot4^x,\) \(x+y+z=16,\) the integral roots in the order \(x,\) \(y,\) \(z\) are:

solutions.explanation:
Since zero is an integer, the case \(x=0\) must be kept when solving the equations. First, rewrite the second equation using powers of \(2\):
\[
2^z=2(2^2)^x=2^{2x+1}.
\]
Distinct integer exponents give distinct powers of \(2\), so \(z=2x+1\). Substituting into \(x+y+z=16\) gives \(y=15-3x\).

If \(x=0\), these relations give \((x,y,z)=(0,15,1)\). The first equation becomes \(1^0=15^0=1\), so this triple satisfies all three equations.

If \(x<0\), write \(x=-n\), where \(n\) is a positive integer. Then \(z=1-2n\) and \(y=15+3n\), both nonzero. Taking absolute values and then reciprocals in the first equation would require
\[
(2n-1)^n=(15+3n)^{2n}.
\]
But \(15+3n>2n-1\geq1\), so \((15+3n)^2>2n-1\). Raising these positive quantities to the power \(n\) shows that the right side is larger. Thus no negative \(x\) works.

If \(x>0\), then \(z=2x+1>0\). The first equation is \(z^x=(y^2)^x\). Equal positive integer powers of nonnegative bases have equal bases, so \(z=y^2\). Therefore
\[
(15-3x)^2=2x+1,
\]
which simplifies and factors as
\[
9x^2-92x+224=(x-4)(9x-56)=0.
\]
The possibilities are \(x=4\) and \(x=56/9\); only \(4\) is an integer. It gives \(y=3\) and \(z=9\). This triple works because \(9^4=3^8\), \(2^9=2\cdot4^4\), and \(4+3+9=16\).

Thus the complete integer solution set is \(\{(0,15,1),(4,3,9)\}\). Choice D is the only listed solution, but the equations have two integer solutions.
solutions.title: Separate zero, negative, and positive exponents
